transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (FinOpsly - Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Eng Manager), Eileen Park (Security)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): weekly POC sync, focus on quality regression in latest batch, discuss prompt tuning and guardrails, plan next evaluation run and security follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can do a quick sync - should be about 45 minutes. Uh, Liam and I will run through the recent test results and proposed fixes. Priya, Carlos, Eileen, can you hear us okay?
[00:12] Priya: Yeah, we can hear you. Sorry, got pulled in from a standup, so I'll mostly be on for the first half.
[00:18] Carlos: All good here.
[00:20] Eileen: loud and clear.

[00:32] Liam: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) recap of latest evaluation (the regression you saw last week), 2) what changed in the prompt sets, 3) proposed guardrails and scoring threshold changes, 4) next run and security follow-up.
[00:44] Priya: perfect. so the big issue is twofold: a small but material drop in accuracy on our negative-sentiment detection and some hallucination on finance-specific entities.
[00:57] Maya: yea, and to add we saw that the tokenization and length distributions also shifted slightly in the last batch - that interacts with the K V cache behavior when using the hosted variant.
[01:10] Carlos: sorry, K V cache? is that K V like cash? the transcript spelled it K V cash last time, so just want to make sure we mean KV cache.
[01:16] Liam: right, yeah KV cache. The runtime's prefix caching and continuous batching can occasionally produce different attention patterns at tail lengths, especially when prompts vary in length.

[01:30] Priya: ok, could you show the failing examples?
[01:33] Liam: sure, I'm gonna share the pilot-results.csv in the chat - link: https://redwood.example/pilot-results/ff-20251007 (note: demo link placeholder). The two examples we flagged: one where the model returns a positive sentiment on a clearly negative merchant dispute, and another where it hallucinated a mitigation step referencing an internal product name 'LedgerX' which isn't in FinOpsly's doc set.
[01:58] Carlos: yeah that LedgerX hallucination is the big one. That would be a customer-facing problem.
[02:04] Maya: quick context — we ran the baseline on Redwood-hosted-inference and a dedicated-quantized variant; the delta was small on average but larger on the tail. The dedicated quantized path had slightly better recall on entity extraction but worse latency at the high concurrency bins.
[02:25] Eileen: from security POV, are any of these changes related to data residency or retention? we have to be sure logs don't include PII before we share with compliance.
[02:35] Liam: good call. The evaluation artifacts are anonymized — pilot-results.csv has redaction, but we'll make a filtered version if you need SOC2-friendly logs.

[02:48] Priya: can we walk through the scoring threshold? our current production threshold is 0.7 for 'actionable' flag; in the test set some borderline cases are hitting 0.68 and were misclassified.
[03:00] Liam: yes, so two levers: raise threshold or add explicit guardrail prompts that ask the model to verify. For example, we tried adding a short verification prompt appended to the user message: \"If you're not sure, answer: uncertain.\" That reduces hallucinations but also increases abstains.
[03:22] Carlos: and that hurts coverage, right? we don't want too many 'uncertain' responses.
[03:26] Maya: correct. The tradeoff is precision vs recall. Our suggestion is incremental: run the guardrail only on low-confidence predictions (0.55-0.75 band) rather than globally.
[03:39] Priya: that sounds reasonable. What's the perf impact?
[03:42] Liam: small - it increases tokens-per-request by ~6-10% for the gated subset. On hosted this is mostly latency-neutral because of batching; on dedicated you see a slight latency bump at p95. We'll include the latency delta in the next CSV.

[03:58] Maya: we also tested a prompt-tuning variant where we reweighted the example set for financial entities — that fixed LedgerX hallucination cases in the sample but introduced a few regressions elsewhere.
[04:12] Priya: hmm ok. do you have the PR curve or confusion matrix?
[04:16] Liam: yes, sliding-window PR curve is in the shared sheet, and confusion matrix snapshots are in the folder too. I'll export a simplified matrix for the top three classes and share.

[04:30] Carlos: what about model variant switching? could we route high-sensitivity traffic to dedicated and noisy traffic to hosted?
[04:41] Maya: absolutely. Smart routing is one of the knobs — route by route or by confidence. You can set policy: high-value customers -> dedicated, default -> hosted, or fallback to a smaller model variant when capacity is constrained.
[04:55] Eileen: for the security deep dive, we need to confirm KMS, audit logs, and SSO details. Maya, can you coordinate the security package?
[05:03] Maya: yes, I'll send over the security packet (SOC2 + ISO + network diagram) and propose times for the CISO call. Link placeholder: https://redwood.example/security-pkg/ff-20251007
[05:15] Eileen: great. Also need an export that shows no PII in the evaluation logs.
[05:20] Liam: we'll produce a redacted export; Priya can confirm before we hand to compliance.

[05:31] Priya: back to guardrails: any chance we can implement a lightweight rule-based prefilter for obvious entity mismatches? like a regex or lookup to catch things that shouldn't appear.
[05:41] Liam: yes, a prefilter is cheap — we recommended a hybrid: rule-based reject for known bad tokens + model-level guardrail for ambiguous cases. That reduces the need to change thresholds broadly.
[05:56] Carlos: ok, timeline — if you re-run the 1k-eval with guardrails, when can we expect results?
[06:03] Liam: I can kick that off today; depending on queue we'll have the CSV and summary by next Tuesday (2025-10-14).
[06:09] Priya: perfect. Also, pricing question — if we go Dedicated for a pilot, what's the expected burn?
[06:14] Maya: I'll send a draft estimate — pilot Dedicated pricing depends on reserved capacity. For a 4-week pilot with moderate throughput we'd propose a small reserved cluster plus burst. I'll include a per-token comparison.
[06:26] Carlos: can you include quantized vs fp16 cost tradeoffs?
[06:29] Maya: yes, we'll include quantization recommendations and expected accuracy deltas.

[06:39] Eileen: small security nuance — we need to validate key management: KMS rotation frequency and HSM availability for the Dedicated option.
[06:49] Liam: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS or HSM integration; we'll chart out options.

[07:00] Priya: any blockers on our side? we need to finalize success criteria: accuracy >= 0.92 on top-3 classes and hallucination rate < 0.5% on the sample.
[07:12] Maya: noted. We'll use that as the pilot pass/fail criteria and run the regression against your top 50 production prompts as a hold-out.

[07:24] Carlos: can Redwood attach model versioning and rollbacks to the pilot so we can pin a version when we go to prod?
[07:31] Liam: yes — version pinning and automatic rollback can be configured; we'll share the rollout policy doc as part of the Ops bundle.

[07:42] Priya: quick question on telemetry retention — how long do logs live by default?
[07:47] Maya: hosted default is 30 days, Dedicated can be configured up to 365 days; compliance add-on for longer retention is available.

[07:57] Eileen: ok please include retention settings in the security packet.
[08:01] Maya: will do.

[08:10] Liam: any other technical asks?
[08:13] Carlos: can you try a run with the guardrail only for the 0.55-0.75 band? that was the main proposal.
[08:20] Liam: yep. I'll set up the eval to gate only that band and include a comparitive column showing abstain vs corrected.

[08:30] Priya: one more ask — please include per-route p95 latency numbers and token costs in the CSV so we can model economics.
[08:36] Maya: yes we'll include per-route cost breakdown and p95.

[08:45] Maya: ok to recap next steps: Liam reruns 1k regression with guardrail for 0.55-0.75 band, outputs CSV + short notes by 2025-10-14; Maya sends pilot pricing and security packet by 2025-10-10; schedule security deep-dive week of 2025-10-20; Priya confirms top 50 prompts & success criteria by 2025-10-13. Anything to add?
[09:08] Priya: nope that's it.
[09:11] Carlos: all good.
[09:13] Eileen: thanks everyone.
[09:15] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in the thread and post updated artifacts.
[09:20] Liam: thanks, bye.

Notes/Artifacts shared in chat: pilot-results.csv (link), rollout-policy.pdf (link), security-pkg (link), per-route-costs.xlsx (link).

End of transcript.
